title: Gyantse
body: Gyantse (Chinese: 江孜, Tibetan: རྒྱལ་རྩེ་), is a city in Xigatse Prefecture.

title: Hocking Hills State Park
body: Hocking Hills State Park and Hocking State Forest are the centerpiece of the Hocking Hills region in Southeast Ohio, in the United States of America.

title: Southern Nevada
body: Southern Nevada is a region of Nevada. Most famous for Las Vegas, this region is also home to Area 51 (the site of classified military research and the subject of UFO conspiracy theories), beautiful rocky canyons, and barren desert landscapes. It comprises Clark County, Esmeralda County, Lincoln County, Mineral County, and Nye County.

title: Dunfermline
body: Dunfermline (Scottish Gaelic: Dùn Phàrlain) is a city in Fife, 3 miles north of the Firth of Forth in central Scotland. The city was a royal residence, ecclesiastical centre and effective capital of Scotland from the 11th century, and many monarchs are buried at its abbey. It's also the birthplace of tycoon philanthropist Andrew Carnegie. In 2022 the population was 55,000.

title: Ragusa (province)
body: Ragusa is a former province in Sicily, Italy, that shares the southeastern tip of the triangular island with Syracuse. Its Baroque towns are a World Heritage Site, and it offers coastal resorts, too.

title: Karamay
body: Karamay (克拉玛依; Kèlāmǎyī) is a city in Xinjiang Province in China. It is famous as an oil base for drilling in the surrounding desert. The oil industry contributes to the city's wealth which is evident in the clean and spacious streets.

title: West Memphis
body: West Memphis is a city in the Delta region of Arkansas, lying across the Mississippi River from Memphis, Tennessee.

title: Moss Beach
body: Moss Beach is a small town on the Pacific Coast on the Peninsula south of San Francisco.

title: Gurugram
body: Gurugram (Hindi: गुरुग्राम Gurugrām) or Gurgaon (गुड़गांव Guṛgā̃v), a satellite city in South Haryana, is a major IT and shopping hub of Delhi. Once a mere commuter town, Gurugram now boasts slick office complexes housing companies from Accenture to Xerox, with more shopping malls per square mile than anywhere else in India. However, the city is also one of the victims of Delhi's unprecedented urban sprawl, with poor infrastructure, traffic jams as well as the winter smog. Despite this, Gurugram often competes with the tech giants like Pune, Hyderabad, or even the IT capital Bengaluru, providing an exhilarating glimpse into the future India. Many Delhiites call it their home.

title: O Grove
body: O Grove is a peninsula, and the main town on that peninsula, linked by a tombola and highway to mainland Galicia in northwest Spain. It's a beach resort and in 2024 had a population of 11,000.

title: Oregon (Ohio)
body: Oregon is a city in Ohio Erie shore west.

title: Isolo
body: Isolo is an area of Lagos in Lagos State, Southwest Nigeria. It is a local council development area (LCDA) under the Oshodi Local Government.

title: Hacker tourism
body: Despite the prevalence of the internet in modern life, there are many resources that are not easily conveyed over a screen. Physical travel can be a great way to gain exposure to unfamiliar technologies, meet online collaborators in the flesh, and pick up some new skills.

title: Nissa
body: Nissa (sometimes spelled as Nisa) is an archaeological site in Ahal Province, Turkmenistan.

title: Batu Pahat
body: Batu Pahat, also called Bandar Penggaram, is a town in Batu Pahat District, Johor, Malaysia.

title: Coon Rapids
body: Coon Rapids is a city in Anoka County, in the Twin Cities region of Minnesota. It is a northern suburb of Minneapolis and home to 63,000 people in 2019.

title: Donghae Coast
body: The Donghae Coast (Korean: 동해 연안) is a region of North Korea stretching along the entire east coast of the North Korean part of the peninsula. It encompasses the provinces of North Hamgyong, South Hamgyong and Kangwon as well as the special Rason city region.

title: Littleton (New Hampshire)
body: Littleton is a city in New Hampshire. Littleton has been featured in a number of magazines in the past decade as particularly attractive, vibrant, welcoming, and resourceful. The downtown area has not deteriorated as have many New England towns when the "Big Box" stores arrived, and retains an authentic charm.

title: Valladolid (Spain)
body: Valladolid is a city in Castile and León in northern Spain, with a population of just over 300,000 in 2024. Much of it is modern and industrial but there's a concentration of sights in its medieval core.

title: Kıyıköy
body: Kıyıköy is a small resort on the Black Sea coast in Eastern Thrace in Turkey. But since 2020 it's been the terminal of a gas pipeline from Russia, so many visitors nowadays are here on business.

title: Wadebridge
body: Wadebridge (Cornish: Ponsrys) is a market town in North Cornwall, with a population of 7,900 (2011). The town sits at the Camel Estuary, 5 miles (8 km) upstream from Padstow. It is host to the Royal Cornwall Agricultural show, each June.

title: Fraser's Hill
body: Fraser's Hill (Bukit Fraser) is a colonial-era hill station in Pahang state, Peninsular Malaysia. Fraser's Hill has a wonderfully weird mixed-up character, where locals eat curries off banana leaves in an English cottage next to a golf course while the call to prayer sounds from the mosque.

title: Mandheera
body: Mandheera county, or Mandera, is the north-eastern-most county in Eastern Kenya. Its capital and largest town is Mandera.

title: Gold Coast/Currumbin
body: Currumbin is a suburb of the Gold Coast, Queensland. For the purpose of this article, this article also includes nearby surrounding suburbs.

title: Chlong
body: Chlong (sometimes spelled Chloung) is a small town in Eastern Cambodia. It serves as a regional centre for the surrounding villages.

title: Isle of Portland
body: For other places with the same name, see Portland (disambiguation). Portland is a town in Dorset, a county on the south coast of the West Country, in England. Portland is actually an island, even though it is linked to the mainland by Chesil Beach, as Chesil Beach is a shoal beach (not a tombolo). Many attractions and facilities are available in the nearby town of Weymouth, a short bus ride away. The area is rapidly improving after the closure of the Naval Base in 1995 with the National Sailing Academy being constructed and holding the London 2012 Olympic sailing events which were staged in Portland Harbour.

title: Barra do Garças
body: Barra do Garças is in Mato Grosso, at the border with Goiás, where the Garças river flows into the mighty Araguaia.

title: Lesmahagow
body: Lesmahagow is a small town in Clydesdale just off M74, with a population of 4300 in 2020. The town name means "the enclosure of St Machutus" (better known as St Malo) though only the Priory foundations remain. Their spiritual successors based here are ISKCON, the Scottish branch of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. A distinguished duo from Lesmahagow were the Cairncross brothers. Sir Alex Cairncross (1911 – 1998) was an economist. John Cairncross (1913 - 1995) was an intelligence officer at Bletchley Park, but recruited by the Soviet Union as a spy. At Cambridge he knew Burgess, Maclean, Philby and Blunt, but it's debateable how much he collaborated with them.

title: Western Galilee
body: The Western Galilee is the most northern coastal region of Israel.

title: Ebor
body: Ebor is a hamlet (population 166 in 2016) in the eastern part of the New England region of New South Wales in Australia.

title: Shishtavec
body: Shishtavec is a village in Kukës County in eastern Albania that represents rich unique folklore, endless varieties of customs, traditions, stories, songs, legends and inspiring landscape. At 1,260 metres above sea level, the village is one of the highest in Albania and a well-known ski area. It is 100 km from Albania's capital, Tirana.

title: North West Coastal Highway
body: The North West Coastal Highway is in Western Australia and runs from Geraldton in the mid-west to Port Hedland in the north. It is part of Highway 1, which loops around Australia, and is an extension of the Brand Highway that runs from near Perth to Geraldton.

title: Hofu
body: Hofu (防府市 Hōfu-shi) is a city in Yamaguchi prefecture, Japan. It is named after its former status as the provincial capital (kokufu 国府) of Suō Province (周防国).

title: Barnstable Village
body: Barnstable village is a village in Barnstable on Cape Cod in Massachusetts. Barnstable village is the most historical of the seven Barnstable villages with an old-time feel due to the many old residences and municipal buildings in the village. Several of Plymouth's surviving Pilgrim families moved here to settle. The village's sheltered harbor made it a natural place for commerce.

title: Carrollton (Georgia)
body: For other places with the same name, see Carrollton (disambiguation). Carrollton is in the West High Country of Georgia.

title: Roquetas de Mar
body: Roquetas de Mar is in Almeria (province). This is a low-key tourist resort town on the Mediterranean coast of Spain, about 18 km from the provincial capital city of Almeria. The town has many long, blue-flag, beaches which are kept meticulously clean. The resort is uncrowded and caters more for families and older travellers than similar resorts on the Costa del Sol. The nightlife is varied but relatively quiet.

title: Wyndham (Western Australia)
body: Wyndham is a town in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, with a population of 914 in 2021. This far northern Kimberley outpost is over 3000 km from the state capital Perth, twice its distance from Bali. That means it has a tropical monsoon climate, with a dry season April-Oct, and the rest of the year is a downpour that only the crocs enjoy.

title: Kishwaukee Valley
body: The Kishwaukee Valley is a region in the greater Northern Illinois area primarily located near the Kishwaukee River's two branches. It includes the entirety of Boone and DeKalb Counties as well as western portions of McHenry County. The Kishwaukee's northern branch rises near Woodstock while the southern branches forms near Shabonna, a rural community south of DeKalb.

title: Cañada de la Virgen
body: Cañada de la Virgen is an archaeological site in the state of Guanajuato, Mexico, about 30 km from the colonial city of San Miguel de Allende. Cañada de la Virgen was built by the Otomi culture around 540 AD as an astronomical observatory. The site reached its peak around the year 900 and was abandoned by 1040. The site includes 3 primary pyramids, several squares or patios, a ballcourt, and numerous smaller structures.

title: Móstoles
body: Móstoles is a city in the Community of Madrid and it is the second largest in the region. Móstoles hosts the CA2M the museum with the contemporary art collection of the Community of Madrid. Historically is also known by the participation of the mayors of the town in the declaration of war against the invasion following the Dos de Mayo Uprasing in 1808.

title: Syrian Desert
body: The Syrian Desert is a vast and sparsely populated region in southeastern Syria. It is the basin of the river Euphrates. It consists of the governorates of Raqqa (Arabic: ‏الرقة), Al-Hasakah (Arabic:الحسكة; Syrian Aramaic: ܓܨܪܛܐ; Kurdish: Hesiça), Deir ez-Zor (Arabic: دير الزور) and parts of the governorates of Homs (Arabic: ‏مُحافظة حمص), Hama (Arabic: ‏محافظة حماة) and Rif Dimashq (Arabic: ریف دمشق).

title: Southend-on-Sea
body: Southend-on-Sea is a seaside resort about 40 miles (64 km) east of London at the mouth of the River Thames Estuary. It's famous for its Victorian pleasure pier, the longest in the world!

title: Palolem
body: Palolem is a village in South Goa, India. Palolem has one of the most beautiful beaches in all of Goa. It is a natural bay surrounded by lofty headlands on either sides, resulting in a calm, idyllic sea with a gently sloping bed which allows you to walk up to 100 m out from the beach.

title: Barnstaple
body: Not to be confused with Barnstable, a city in Massachusetts, United States of America. Barnstaple is a town of 32,000 people (2018) in North Devon, England.

title: Dubai/Jumeirah
body: Within Jumeirah you'll find most of the tourist attractions that modern Dubai has to offer. Nonetheless the majority of its territory consists of residential and commercial areas. This article also covers the Palm and World Islands off the coast of Dubai.

title: Hamina
body: Hamina is a town in Kymenlaakso, in the extreme southeast of Finland.

title: Korean palaces
body: In monarchical states, the power of the king was absolute, and life within the palace revolved around him under strict norms. The lifestyle therein was often the most sophisticated and luxurious. Historically, there are numerous magnificent palaces such as the Forbidden City and Versailles, which are globally recognized for their historical importance and symbolic significance. In South Korea, only palaces from the Joseon Dynasty have fully retained their original appearance. However, this does not diminish the historical significance or touristic value of palaces from other dynasties. Palaces from non-Joseon dynasties also possess considerable historical value and significance. Although Korean palaces were influenced by China, they are not overly extravagant but rather modestly designed with a focus on harmonizing with nature.

title: Diving the Cape Peninsula and False Bay/Hout Bay harbour
body: Hout Bay is one of the diving areas of the Cape Peninsula and False Bay. Its harbour slipway is used by divers mostly in summer, when south easterly wind makes diving on the False Bay side of the peninsula unpleasant.

title: Llandudno
body: For other places with the same name, see Llandudno (disambiguation). Llandudno is a Victorian-era seaside resort situated on the picturesque north coast of Wales. Once a favourite of Queen Victoria, Llandudno still retains an old-world charm that sets it aside from other British seaside resorts. Llandudno is set between the cities of Bangor and Chester and is easily accessible by road and rail.

title: Pristina
body: Pristina (Albanian: Prishtinë or definite form Prishtina, Serbian: Priština), the capital and largest city of Kosovo: it is messy, with centuries-old Ottoman heritage competing with communist designs and post-communist architectural buildings. However, there is a powerful draw to this city of 227,000 people (2024), offering much to passing visitors.

title: Sydney/Outer West
body: The Outer West is the huge western area of Sydney that includes the suburbs of Blacktown, Mt. Druitt, St. Mary's and Penrith.

title: Nome (Alaska)
body: Nome is a city in the Arctic region of Alaska. It is a town of about 4,000 people, about half of whom are Alaska Natives. It is the transportation and commerce center for Northwest Alaska. It is also the western terminus of the Iditarod Trail.

title: Smarhon
body: Smarhon (Smarhon’, Smorgon’, Smorgonie) is a town in Grodno Oblast, Belarus.

title: Taipei/Shilin
body: Shihlin (士林區) is a northern district of Taipei, home to many museums and one of Taipei's largest night markets.

title: Pitres
body: Pitres is a small town in the province of Granada, in the La Tahá municipality, in Andalucia (or Andalusia), Spain. The other main towns in the area are Mecina Fondales and Ferreirola, but Pitres is La Tahá's economic and governmental center. The area forms a part of La Alpujarra Nearby towns of similar character: Portugos and Busquistar

title: Jardín
body: Jardín is a town located in the southernmost part of the department of Antioquia. Unlike many other hamlets in the country, Jardín has remained largely unchanged since established in 1864. Less than 20,000 people inhabit Jardín, in the past most dedicated their lives to growing coffee, plantains, beans and sugarcane. Today many will be glad to show you their town and surroundings. Mean daily temperatures are 19°C with moderate humidity. Days are comfortable while nights are colder and a jacket or sweater is required. The area of the municipality is 224 km² (87 mi²).

title: Franconian Switzerland
body: The Franconian Switzerland (German: Fränkische Schweiz) is an upland in Franconia, northern Bavaria and a popular tourist retreat. It is one of the oldest and most popular holiday areas in Germany.

title: Tramping in New Zealand
body: Tramping (known in other countries as hiking, trekking or bushwalking) is a popular way to see the New Zealand outdoors, especially the forests, mountains and other wilderness areas. Tramps range from day walks to multi-day hikes, sleeping in huts or perhaps camping out. Most national parks in New Zealand are administered by the Department of Conservation (usually abbreviated to and often just called DOC). DOC offices and their web site are very useful sources of information.

title: Diving in Mozambique/Xstacy Reef
body: The dive site Xstacy Reef is an offshore rocky reef with coral in the Guinjata Bay area near Inhambane in Southern Mozambique.

title: Intercity buses in Germany
body: While most European countries have had a system of long distance buses for a long time, intercity bus travel was virtually nonexistent in Germany until 2012. Things have changed rapidly since then and intercity buses are now a relatively cheap way to get to a wide range of German and a handful of international destinations.
